finding.title: Split or trim hand-written progress widget files over the 400-line AG-3 cap
finding.why: lifetime_folder_styled_widgets.dart is 650 lines (62% over the cap) and bundles a theme/gradient constants class with six unrelated standalone widget classes plus an enum in one file — the kind of file where an unrelated one-line style tweak forces a reviewer to scroll past six other widgets' worth of unrelated diff. siyumim_grouped_view.dart (437), curriculum_breakdown_list.dart (413) and monthly_activity_sliver_calendar.dart (404, also dead — see companion finding) are more modestly over (1-9%).
finding.recommendation: Split lifetime_folder_styled_widgets.dart along its class boundaries (e.g. lifetime_folder_gradients.dart, lifetime_folder_surface.dart, lifetime_marking_scope_row.dart); trim the other three opportunistically on next touch.
acceptance_criteria: A line-count checker (tool/ script or CI grep) enumerates these 4 paths today and is wired into make audit per Rule 0; count drops to 0 after the split.

finding.title: Stop pinning the dead, unlocalized ChartTimeRange.displayName getter with a coverage-chasing test
finding.why: chart_data_test.dart's own header says it exists to 'cover' previously-uncovered lines — its four tests simply assert the literal English strings the source hardcodes ('7 Days'/'30 Days'/'All Time'), the textbook tautological pattern (compare-against-what-the-source-literally-returns). Worse, the getter under test is dead: the only real caller, recent_activity_screen.dart, ignores ChartTimeRange.displayName entirely and switches through proper AppLocalizations getters (l10n.chartLast7Days etc.) instead. So this test spends 25 lines locking in a hardcoded-English getter that (a) no production code calls and (b) would violate AX-2 the moment anyone wired it up, and its passing status gives false confidence.
finding.recommendation: Delete chart_data_test.dart together with the ChartTimeRange.displayName getter itself, since recent_activity_screen.dart already has the correct localized replacement — don't keep a passing test whose only job is protecting a hardcoded-English string from ever being fixed.
acceptance_criteria: Either ChartTimeRange.displayName and its test are removed, or the getter is rebuilt on AppLocalizations and the test asserts against l10n fixtures instead of literal English.

finding.title: Consolidate the near-duplicate chart_data_service test files spawned across fix waves
finding.rule: Fowler duplication / AG-5 (one mirrored test suite per source file)

evidence.quote: test('returns null when goal has no targetDate', () async {
test('returns null when the goal has no targetDate', () async {
test('bulkInTrack rows: INCLUDED on the chart (W1-B / Phase A)', () async {

finding.why: chart_data_service.dart (697 lines) is covered by FIVE test files totalling ~1,643 lines, and two independent near-duplicate pairs formed inside that set. extended_test.dart and extra_test.dart both claim to add getTargetLine coverage and reimplement the same five cases (null-no-goal, null-no-targetDate, zero-days, happy-path length, monotonic-increase) with their own copies of the same setUp/insertGoal helpers. migration_test.dart and sentinel_test.dart both re-verify the identical W1-B trackAchievement-tier behavior (bulkInTrack charted, lifetimeOnly excluded, live+bulk mixed) for the same two methods, down to near-identical doc-comment framing of the same fix wave. Each pair has exactly one genuinely unique case (extra_test's baselineCount-excludes-pre-goal-completions; sentinel_test's sentinel-timestamp-without-import-record test). This is fix-wave churn: a coverage request spawned a new file instead of extending the existing suite, so the service now needs two files edited in lockstep for the same behavior and the copies can silently drift apart.
finding.recommendation: Fold extra_test.dart's one unique case into chart_data_service_extended_test.dart and delete extra_test.dart; fold sentinel_test.dart's sentinel-timestamp case into chart_data_service_migration_test.dart and delete sentinel_test.dart.
acceptance_criteria: chart_data_service has at most 3 test files after consolidation.
The two currently-unique cases (baselineCount-excludes-pre-goal completions; sentinel-without-import treated as live) still exist and pass in the retained files.
No expect( count regresses across the merge (TQ-7 ratchet).

finding.title: Add a semantic label to the icon-only drill-in IconButton in LifetimeMarkingScopeRow
finding.why: This IconButton has no tooltip and isn't wrapped in Semantics, unlike the rest of the batch — progress_tier_counter_row.dart, for example, explicitly wraps its icon+number tiles in Semantics(label: ...). A screen-reader user landing on this control hears an unlabeled button with no indication it drills into the row's children.
finding.recommendation: Add a tooltip (e.g. an l10n 'View details' / drill-in key) to the IconButton.
acceptance_criteria: The IconButton exposes a non-empty accessible label (tooltip or Semantics wrapper), verifiable via a widget test asserting on Semantics data.

finding.title: Rename one of the two unrelated PaceIndicator classes (progress vs scheduler features)
finding.rule: AG-4 (public top-level symbol names unique across lib/)
finding.why: Two entirely different widgets share the class name PaceIndicator: progress's takes a PaceCalculator plus an optional subtitleCaption and renders a full card; scheduler's takes a bare PaceStatus and renders a compact dot+label row. Different constructors mean no compile error today, but any grep/'find usages'/agent-generated new call site has a real chance of picking the wrong one, and the two can't be imported into the same file without an alias.
finding.recommendation: Rename one (e.g. scheduler's to CompactPaceIndicator, matching its actual inline-row shape) to keep the symbol space unambiguous.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn 'class PaceIndicator' lib/ returns exactly one match.
